input.family: "type" keyword and the underlying type system (Draft7Validator + ErrorTree), test18_executable

rules.rule: Output shape is fixed: line1=ErrorTree.total_errors, line2=line3=raw len(iter_errors), lines4-6 = Python bool literal `True`/`False` (capital T/F) and always equal to (rawCount==0), lines7-8 = literal `None`, lines9-10 = same value as line1. Exit 0. Any exception anywhere => completely EMPTY stdout, exit 1 (argparse failures give exit 2).
A failing `type` keyword produces EXACTLY ONE error at that instance node, regardless of how many type names are listed in the array.

Type membership table (instance -> which of the 7 names it satisfies): null->null; true/false->boolean ONLY (never number, never integer); JSON object->object; JSON array->array; string->string; int literal->number AND integer; float literal->number, and ALSO integer iff its float value has zero fractional part.

Draft7 zero-fraction rule details: -0.0, 1e2, 1.0e0, 1e308 are all `integer`. 0.1 and -1.5 are not. 1.00000000000000001 and 1.0000000000000000000000001 ARE integer (they round to 1.0 in float64, so test the PARSED double, not the source text).

Overflowing float literals become Infinity: 1e400 / -1e400 / Infinity / -Infinity are `number` but NOT `integer`. NaN is `number` but NOT `integer`. (Python json.loads accepts the bare tokens NaN, Infinity, -Infinity — a strict JSON.parse in JS will throw instead; you must special-case these tokens.)
Integers are arbitrary precision and EXACT — no float64 rounding. Comparisons (const/enum/maximum) on >2^53 integers must be done with BigInt/decimal-string semantics in JS.

ErrorTree collapse key = (absolute instance path, validator keyword). Two errors sharing BOTH collapse into one; different keyword at the same path does NOT collapse. total_errors is computed recursively: node.total = (#distinct keywords among errors whose remaining path is empty at this node) + sum(child.total).

rules.rule: anyOf / oneOf / not / contains / if-then wrap their sub-errors: they emit exactly ONE error at the parent node (children are not surfaced by iter_errors), so no collapse and count is 1.
allOf and $ref do NOT wrap: their sub-errors are surfaced individually with the parent's instance path, which is the main source of collapse.

`type` MUST be either a simpleType string or a non-empty array of UNIQUE simpleType strings, ANYWHERE in the schema (including unreached subschemas, `definitions`, and `not`). Otherwise check_schema raises SchemaError => EMPTY, exit 1. Legal names are exactly: null, boolean, object, array, number, string, integer (case-sensitive, no surrounding whitespace).
rules.evidence: '{"type":[]}' -> EMPTY exit=1 (SchemaError: [] is not valid under any of the given schemas, metaschema['properties']['type'] minItems 1) ; '{"type":["integer","integer"]}' -> EMPTY exit=1 (uniqueItems) ; '{"type":"Integer"}', '{"type":"int"}', '{"type":"NUMBER"}', '{"type":"integer "}', '{"type":" integer"}', '{"type":{}}' -> EMPTY exit=1 ; --a 1 --b '{"type":"integer","definitions":{"x":{"type":"int"}}}' -> EMPTY exit=1 ; --a 1 --b '{"type":"integer","not":{"type":"int"}}' -> EMPTY exit=1

rules.rule: Evaluation ORDER is observable: iter_errors runs BEFORE check_schema (test18.py line 17 vs line 33). The unknown-type lookup inside `type` is a short-circuiting any(), so an unknown type name only raises UnknownType at iter_errors if it is actually REACHED (i.e. no earlier listed name matched the instance). Otherwise the SchemaError from check_schema fires instead. Both give EMPTY exit 1, so the distinction is only visible on stderr — a JS reimplementation can treat all invalid `type` as exit 1.

rules.rule: Sibling keywords are applied INDEPENDENTLY of a failing `type`; a type error does not suppress other keyword errors at the same node. Each applicable keyword adds its own error.
Each keyword self-gates on the instance's type and silently passes for non-applicable types. Booleans are exempt from ALL numeric keywords (they are not `number`).

rules.rule: Equality for const/enum/uniqueItems: 1 == 1.0 (numeric equality, cross int/float), but booleans are NEVER equal to numbers, at any nesting depth (special bool-vs-number guard in the deep comparison).
String length is measured in Unicode CODE POINTS (Python semantics), not UTF-16 units. An astral character counts as 1.

Schema must be a JSON object or a JSON boolean. `true` = always valid, `false` = 1 error at the node. Any other top-level schema JSON (array, null, string, number) crashes during Draft7Validator construction/first use with AttributeError/TypeError from referencing/_legacy_dollar_id => EMPTY exit 1.

rules.rule: Unknown/misspelled keywords are ignored (no error, no schema error). Keyword names are case-sensitive.

`$schema` is ignored for dialect selection — Draft-7 semantics and the Draft-7 metaschema are always used, even for a draft-04 or bogus $schema value. Consequently draft-04-only forms like boolean `exclusiveMinimum` are a SchemaError.

rules.rule: Instance JSON parsing uses Python json.loads: duplicate object keys -> last one wins; leading/trailing whitespace OK; lone surrogates in \uXXXX escapes are accepted; but leading zeros (01), single quotes, `undefined`, and empty string are parse errors => EMPTY exit 1.

rules.rule: Array-index and object-key path components both key the ErrorTree; per-item/per-property errors do NOT collapse across different indices/keys.
A node's own error and its descendants' errors both count toward total_errors (parent contributes its own keyword set plus the recursive sum of children).

rules.rule: argparse artifact, not program logic: a value beginning with '-' that does not match ^-\d+$ or ^-\d*\.\d+$ is treated as an option and the process exits 2 with EMPTY stdout. Use --a=<value>. Missing --a/--b or no args also exit 2.
rules.evidence: --a '-1e400' --b '{"type":"integer"}' -> EMPTY exit=2 ; --a='-1e400' --b '{"type":"integer"}' -> 1,1,1,False,...  ; --a '-0.0' (space form) works -> 0,...,True ; --a '-Infinity' -> EMPTY exit=2 but --a='-Infinity' -> 0,...,True ; missing --b -> exit=2 ; no args -> exit=2

surprises: `1.0` IS an `integer` in Draft 7 (any float with zero fractional part), including -0.0, 1e2, 1e308, and 1.00000000000000001 (which rounds to 1.0). A naive JS `Number.isInteger` check on the raw token, or a 'has a decimal point => not integer' rule, gets this wrong.

`1e400` and `NaN` are `number` but NOT `integer` (they become inf/nan and fail is_integer). Also, Python json.loads ACCEPTS the bare tokens NaN, Infinity, -Infinity, which strict JSON.parse in JS rejects.

Booleans are never `number`/`integer`, AND they are exempt from every numeric/string/array/object keyword — `true` validates clean against {"minimum":5,"multipleOf":2,"maxLength":0,"minItems":3,"required":["a"]}.

Integers are arbitrary precision: 10000000000000000001 != 10000000000000000000 and 9007199254740993 != 9007199254740992. JS Number collapses both pairs, so const/enum/maximum comparisons need BigInt or string-based comparison.

ErrorTree collapses by (path, keyword): {"allOf":[{"type":"string"},{"type":"number"},{"type":"array"}]} on null gives line1=1 but line2=3. allOf and $ref surface child errors at the parent path (collapsible); anyOf/oneOf/not/contains/if-then wrap into a single parent error (never collapsible).

An unknown type NAME anywhere in the schema — even in `definitions` or inside a `not` that is logically irrelevant — kills the whole run (exit 1), because check_schema validates the entire schema against the Draft-7 metaschema. But whether the failure comes from iter_errors (UnknownType) or check_schema (SchemaError) depends on the short-circuiting any(): {"type":["string","int"]} raises UnknownType for instance 1 and SchemaError for instance "x".

`type` values that are ints/null/bools crash with TypeError 'not iterable' inside the type keyword BEFORE check_schema, while `type: {}` does not (a dict is iterable over its keys) and instead fails at check_schema. Duplicate entries ({"type":["integer","integer"]}) and empty arrays ({"type":[]}) are metaschema violations, not validation failures.
String lengths are code points, so "😀" satisfies {"maxLength":1} and violates {"minLength":2}; JS `.length` gives 2 and inverts both results.
A top-level schema of `[]`, `null`, `"x"`, or `1` crashes at validator construction (referencing/_legacy_dollar_id), not at validation — but `true`/`false` are perfectly valid boolean schemas.

$schema is completely ignored for dialect selection: a draft-04 $schema still gets Draft-7 semantics and is still checked against the Draft-7 metaschema (so draft-04's boolean exclusiveMinimum is a hard SchemaError).
